title: Interaction of Supernova Ejecta with Nearby Protoplanetary Disks
direct_prompt: The interaction of supernova ejecta with nearby protoplanetary disks is a topic of significant interest in the field of astronomy and astrophysics. The explosive death of massive stars can send shock waves and high-energy particles through the interstellar medium, potentially impacting the formation and evolution of young planetary systems. In this review, we discuss the various mechanisms through which supernova ejecta can interact with protoplanetary disks, including direct impacts, shock heating, and chemical enrichment. We also examine observational evidence for such interactions, such as anomalous isotopic ratios in meteorites and the presence of supernova-produced elements in young stellar systems. Additionally, we explore theoretical models and simulations that investigate the effects of supernova interactions on disk structure and planet formation. Our analysis highlights the potential for supernovae to both disrupt and enhance the evolution of protoplanetary disks, ultimately influencing the diversity of planetary systems that may form in the aftermath of stellar explosions. Continued study of these interactions is crucial for understanding the complex interplay between supernovae, protoplanetary disks, and the formation of planetary systems. Future observations and theoretical advancements will provide valuable insights into the role of supernovae in shaping the early stages of planet formation and the diversity of exoplanetary systems in the galaxy.

Previous models ofSolar System formation considered a supernova shock that triggered the collapseof the Sun's nascent molecular cloud. We advocate an alternative hypothesis,that the Solar System's protoplanetary disk had already formed when a veryclose (< 1 pc) supernova injected radioactive material directly into the disk.We conduct the first numerical simulations designed to answer two questionsrelated to this hypothesis: will the disk be destroyed by such a closesupernova; and will any of the ejecta be mixed into the disk? Our simulationsdemonstrate that the disk does not absorb enough momentum from the shock toescape the protostar to which it is bound. Only low amounts (< 1%) of mass lossoccur, due to stripping by Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities across the top of thedisk, which also mix into the disk about 1% of the intercepted ejecta. direct_prompt: Lyman Break Galaxies (LBGs) are galaxies observed at high redshift (z > 3) through the Lyman break technique. They are among the earliest galaxies in the Universe and are thought to be the progenitors of massive galaxies in the local Universe.We present deep rest-frame UV spectra of five LBGs at z ~ 5. These spectra are among the deepest rest-frame UV spectra of LBGs to date and allow us to study the properties of these galaxies in detail.Our analysis reveals that these LBGs are very compact, have low stellar masses, and are forming stars at a high rate. We also find evidence for outflows in these galaxies, suggesting that they are undergoing feedback from star formation.Our results provide new insights into the properties of LBGs at z ~ 5. These galaxies are the building blocks of massive galaxies in the local Universe, and our study helps to shed light on their early evolution.
prompt_few_shot: The rest-frame UV spectra of a large sample of Lyman break galaxies (LBGs) at z~5 are investigated with the aim of understanding the physical properties of LBGs. We have constructed a sample of 161 LBGs with z~5, selected on the basis of deep U-band imaging and confirmed by spectroscopy. We find that the equivalent widths (EWs) of the C IV lambda1549 and He II lambda1640 emission lines decrease with decreasing UV continuum luminosity, indicating a luminosity-dependent ionization parameter. The faintest LBGs tend to have lower EWs of C IV and He II, and weaker [O III] emission, indicating that they are less active and more chemically unevolved than the brighter LBGs. We find a tight correlation between the EWs of C IV and He II, suggesting that they arise in similar regions of the galaxies. We compare the LBGs with model predictions and find that they are consistent with being a mix of star-forming and composite (i.e., star-forming + active galactic nucleus) systems. The composite fraction among LBGs is found to be 24^{+12}_{-8}%. The mass-to-light ratios of LBGs estimated from the observed spectral energy distributions are consistent with the values expected for young stellar populations, suggesting that LBGs are dominated by recent star formation. The observed UV spectral properties of LBGs can be explained by the presence of a young, massive stellar population and a low-level of dust extinction.

By exploring the dynamics of neural networks in relation to behavior, this study provides valuable insights into the complexities of human responses to aversive stimuli. Furthermore, the findings offer potential implications for the development of interventions aimed at regulating responses to aversive stimuli. Overall, this research contributes to the growing body of literature on the neural mechanisms underlying behavioral responses to aversive stimuli.

title: Zero-temperature resistive transition in Josephson-junction arrays at  irrational frustration
direct_prompt: In this study, we investigate the zero-temperature resistive transition in Josephson-junction arrays with irrational frustration. We find that the presence of irrational frustration leads to unique behaviors in the resistive transition of the system. Our results show that the critical current of the array exhibits non-monotonic behavior as a function of frustration strength, with distinct peaks at specific irrational values. Additionally, we observe a suppression of the critical current near these irrational values, indicating a novel mechanism for controlling the resistive transition in Josephson-junction arrays. Through detailed numerical simulations, we demonstrate the robustness of these findings and provide insights into the underlying physical mechanisms driving the zero-temperature resistive transition in these systems. Our results have implications for the design and optimization of Josephson-junction arrays for various applications in quantum information processing and superconducting electronics.

direct_prompt: Here is a 9 sentence academic article abstract for the given title:Collaborative tagging allows users to freely assign keywords, or tags, to resources in online communities to help with organization and discovery. This study aimed to explore how user attention is directed when tagging collaboratively. An analysis was conducted of tagging activity on a major academic bookmarking website over a one year period. Data on the tags users assigned and which resources they viewed was anonymously logged. Preliminary results suggest that users tend to focus their attention on resources tagged by other highly active users within the site. Additionally, popular or frequently assigned tags seem to draw more views to the resources they are applied to. The network of tags created by users and the flow of attention between tags and resources forms a complex tangled hierarchy. Further analysis sought to map how attention propagates through this network over time and how influential some tags and users become as attractors of attention. The findings provide insights into how collaborative communities self-organize towards consensus on describing shared content through emergent folksonomies and attention flows.

title: Compact starburst in the central regions of Seyfert galaxies
direct_prompt: In this study, we investigate the properties of compact starbursts in the central regions of Seyfert galaxies using a combination of multiwavelength observations and simulations. We find that these starbursts are characterized by high surface brightness, young ages, and low metallicities, indicative of a burst of star formation triggered by the interaction with the galactic nucleus. The starbursts are spatially correlated with the ionized gas and dust lanes, suggesting a causal link between the two. Our results suggest that the compact starbursts play a key role in the evolution of Seyfert galaxies, and may be an important mechanism for fueling the active galactic nucleus. Further study of these starbursts may provide valuable insights into the coevolution of galaxies and supermassive black holes.

Furthermore, we highlight areas where further research is needed to gain a more comprehensive understanding of this fundamental aspect of human genome biology.

title: The effect of the relative orientation between the coronal field and new  emerging flux: I Global Properties
direct_prompt: [assistant]: The Sun's coronal magnetic field is structured by the continuous emergence of new magnetic flux from the solar interior. The interaction between new emerging flux and pre-existing coronal magnetic fields has long been considered a fundamental process in solar coronal heating. The relative orientation between the pre-existing coronal field and newly emerging flux is a crucial factor in determining the interaction's outcome. In this work, we investigate the statistical properties of the relative orientation between the coronal field and emerging flux by analyzing a large sample of emerging flux regions. We show that the probability distribution of the relative orientation angle between the coronal field and emerging flux is strongly peaked around 90 degrees, indicating a preferred perpendicular orientation. We also find that the distribution of the relative orientation angle is modulated by the magnetic complexity of the surrounding corona, with a larger dispersion of the relative orientation angle in regions with more complex magnetic fields. Our results provide observational constraints on the relative orientation between the coronal field and emerging flux and have implications for understanding the interaction between them.

direct_prompt: TrES Exoplanets and False Positives: Finding the Needle in the Haystack.**Abstract:** Exoplanet surveys, especially those in the transit method, are prone to false positives. It is a crucial issue that affects the statistics of exoplanet populations. The Trans-atlantic Exoplanet Survey (TrES) discovered four transiting exoplanets orbiting the stars GSC 02622-00842, GSC 03089-00929, GSC 03543-01430, and GSC 03830-01057. Among these, TrES-4 and TrES-3 have been confirmed through radial velocities, while TrES-2 and TrES-1 have not. We use extensive photometric observations to search for possible astrophysical false positives in the TrES data. We do not find any evidence to suggest that these signals are due to phenomena other than transiting planets. Combining our photometric data with previously published radial velocities, we refine the system parameters and determine that the planetary nature of TrES-2 and TrES-1 is secure.We also discuss the general problem of false positives in exoplanet surveys and argue that several methods exist to efficiently weed out false signals.

However, many potential transits are actually false positives, caused by other astrophysical phenomena such as eclipsing binary stars. The TrES (Trans-atlantic Exoplanet Survey) project, which uses a network of small telescopes to search for transiting exoplanets, has developed a number of techniques to distinguish between true transits and false positives. These techniques include analyzing the shape of the transit light curve, the color of the star, and the presence of additional eclipses. By carefully applying these techniques, the TrES team has been able to identify a number of new exoplanets, including several "hot Jupiters" (gas giants orbiting very close to their stars) and a number of smaller, Earth-like planets.

title: Possible X-ray diagnostic for jet/disk dominance in Type 1 AGN
direct_prompt: Active galactic nuclei (AGN) are complex astronomical objects that emit high-energy radiation, often in the form of X-rays. Type 1 AGN are characterized by the presence of broad emission lines in their spectra, which are believed to originate from gas clouds close to the supermassive black hole at the center of the galaxy. In this study, we propose a possible X-ray diagnostic tool to determine the relative dominance of the jet or accretion disk in Type 1 AGN. By analyzing the X-ray spectral properties of a sample of Type 1 AGN, we found that the ratio of the X-ray luminosity in the soft and hard bands can provide valuable information about the underlying physical processes in these systems. Specifically, a higher soft X-ray luminosity relative to the hard X-ray luminosity is indicative of a dominant accretion disk, while a higher hard X-ray luminosity suggests a dominant jet. Our results suggest that this X-ray diagnostic can help classify Type 1 AGN based on their underlying physical mechanisms. Furthermore, our findings provide valuable insights into the connection between accretion disk and jet activity in AGN and shed light on the processes that drive the high-energy emission observed in these systems. Further observational and theoretical studies are needed to confirm and expand on these results, with the ultimate goal of better understanding the complex nature of AGN and their role in galaxy evolution.

title: The SSS phase of RS Ophiuchi observed with Chandra and XMM-Newton I.:  Data and preliminary Modeling
direct_prompt: The paper presents the first results of a Chandra and XMM-Newton monitoring campaign of the recurrent nova RS Ophiuchi during its 2021 outburst. This campaign was triggered by the detection of a very early X-ray maximum by Swift/BAT on July 8, 2021, 5 days after the optical outburst. The unprecedented early and frequent X-ray monitoring allowed us to follow, for the first time, the temporal and spectral evolution of the very early phases of the RS Oph 2021 outburst. We analyze here the data collected by Chandra and XMM-Newton during the first week of the outburst, that is, during the so-called SSS phase, when the ejecta are still homologously expanding and the reverse shock is propagating inward. The main results of our analysis are the following: (i) the X-ray emission during this phase is dominated by thermal emission from the shocked ejecta; (ii) during the first 2 days, the X-ray emission is optically thick, and we observe a clear decrease in the column density; (iii) a power-law component is present in addition to the thermal emission; (iv) the abundances of the ejecta are similar to those of the solar atmosphere, with possibly overabundant O and Ne; (v) we find evidence that the absorbing material is likely clumpy with clumps of overabundant O and Ne.

direct_prompt: [Abstract]: In this paper, we study the asymptotic properties of duration-driven long-range dependent (LDR) processes. We consider a general class of LDR processes, including fractional Brownian motion and fractional Gaussian noise, and derive their asymptotic distributions under various conditions. Our results provide a comprehensive understanding of the limiting behavior of duration-driven LDR processes, which can be useful in a variety of applications, such as telecommunications, queuing theory, and finance.Specifically, we first establish the weak convergence of duration-driven LDR processes to a Gaussian process. We then derive the exact form of the limiting Gaussian process and characterize its properties. Furthermore, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the sample mean and sample variance of duration-driven LDR processes and obtain their limiting distributions. Our results are derived using a combination of techniques from probability theory and functional analysis.

However, parallel manipulators also experience complex inverse kinematic solutions with multiple posture solutions within their workspaces. This presents challenges in controlling the end effector movement and posture. This article presents a novel method to identify uniqueness domains, which are continuous regions where the inverse kinematics has a unique solution. The uniqueness domains are extracted through an optimization process that maximizes their sizes within the overall workspace. The approach is demonstrated on two common types of 3 degree of freedom parallel manipulators. The results show the capability to identify uniquely-solvable regions of moderate sizes within their workspaces. Identifying these uniqueness domains provides valuable information to trajectory planning and control algorithms for parallel manipulators. The method offers a new systematic way to analyze the inverse kinematic properties within the workspaces of parallel manipulator designs.

title: Jet-disturbed molecular gas near the Seyfert 2 nucleus in M51
direct_prompt: The Seyfert 2 nucleus in the spiral galaxy M51 is known to host a turbulent environment characterized by the presence of jet-disturbed molecular gas. This study investigates the properties of this molecular gas and its association with the central black hole activity. High-resolution observations using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) reveal clumpy structures in the molecular gas distribution located close to the nucleus. These clumps show signatures of velocity gradients and are asymmetrically distributed with respect to the radio jet axis. The kinematics of the molecular gas suggest interactions with the radio jet, possibly due to shocks generated by the jet propagation through the interstellar medium. In addition, the molecular gas shows indications of being ionized, which may result from the impact of the jet on the gas. The presence of jet-disturbed molecular gas near the Seyfert 2 nucleus in M51 provides insights into the interplay between the active galactic nucleus and its surrounding gas dynamics. Further studies are needed to fully understand the impact of the radio jet on the molecular gas properties and its implications for the evolution of the central region in M51.

title: Characterization of P2P IPTV Traffic: Scaling Analysis
direct_prompt: In this paper, we investigate the scaling properties of P2P IPTV traffic, a rapidly growing segment of online multimedia streaming. By analyzing a large trace dataset, we identify key features of P2P IPTV traffic and examine its scaling behavior using various techniques. Our results show that P2P IPTV traffic exhibits a power-law distribution in terms of session durations, and follows a stretched-exponential pattern in terms of packet inter-arrival times. We also find that the traffic displays a high degree of temporal and spatial locality, with a significant fraction of packets belonging to a few popular streams. Furthermore, we observe a strong correlation between the number of peers and the stream popularity, suggesting a hierarchical structure in the P2P overlay. Our findings have important implications for the design and optimization of P2P IPTV systems, and highlight the need for further research in understanding the underlying mechanisms and dynamics of this emerging technology.

In this paper, we conduct a comprehensive analysis of P2P IPTV traffic to understand its characteristics and scaling properties. Our analysis reveals that P2P IPTV traffic exhibits a highly skewed distribution, with a small number of popular channels absorbing the majority of the traffic. We also find that the traffic demand for P2P IPTV is highly predictable, allowing for efficient caching and content delivery strategies. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of different factors such as peer density, video quality, and network conditions on P2P IPTV traffic. Our results show that increasing peer density and video quality leads to a significant increase in traffic, while improving network conditions has a marginal effect. Finally, we propose a scalable architecture for P2P IPTV that can handle large numbers of users and channels while maintaining high video quality.

title: UV Star Formation Rates in the Local Universe
direct_prompt: Here is a 14 sentence abstract for the paper title "UV Star Formation Rates in the Local Universe":UV light from young, massive stars is a direct tracer of the formation of new stars within galaxies. We analyze UV photometric observations of galaxies in the local Universe from the GALEX All-Sky Survey to estimate star formation rates (SFRs) based on the UV luminosity. The GALEX dataset provides UV observations of over 50,000 galaxies within 200 Mpc, allowing us to study star formation across a broad range of galaxy types and masses. We discuss various methods for converting UV luminosity to SFR and compare the results to SFR measurements from H-alpha and infrared observations. Our SFRs based on UV luminosity are overall consistent with other tracers but show more variation for low-mass, low SFR galaxies. We examine how SFR scales with key galaxy properties like stellar mass, morphology, and environment. Across multiple environments, we find a relation between stellar mass and specific SFR. Less massive galaxies typically have higher specific SFRs. Using group catalogs, we analyze how SFR depends on a galaxy's position within its dark matter halo and proximity to neighboring galaxies. On average, satellite galaxies have lower SFRs than centrals of the same stellar mass. This work provides a comprehensive characterization of the current rates of star formation across the local galaxy population as traced by UV emission.

title: Multi-wavelength analysis of 18um-selected galaxies in the AKARI/IRC  monitor field towards the North Ecliptic Pole
direct_prompt: Multi-wavelength analysis of 18um-selected galaxies in the AKARI/IRC monitor field toward the North Ecliptic PoleWe present multi-wavelength properties of galaxies selected at 18um in the AKARI North Ecliptic Pole (NEP) field with coverage in optical, near-infrared (NIR), mid-infrared (MIR), and radio wavelengths. The AKARI NEP-Wide field (NEP-W1, 0.66 deg2) is covered with the Subaru/Hyper Suprime-Cam in five broad bands (B, V, r, i, z), and with the UKIRT/WFCAM in the NIR (J, H, K bands) and also with the Spitzer/MIPS in the MIR (24um). Deep radio observations were obtained at 1.4 GHz with the VLA. Counterparts at other wavelengths are identified for 86% of the 18um sources in the NEP-W1 field. Optical and NIR colors of the 18um-selected galaxies are similar to those of general galaxies at similar redshifts. Galaxies with red colors in the optical and NIR have higher 24um flux densities. About 50% of the 18um-selected galaxies have optical spectroscopic redshifts. The redshift distribution of the 18um sources peaks at z ~ 0.3 and extends to z ~ 1.5. The space density of the 18um-selected galaxies in the NEP-W1 field is consistent with that of the general galaxy population with similar luminosities and redshifts. The radio-loudness (defined by the ratio of 1.4 GHz flux density to 24um flux density) of the 18um-selected galaxies is comparable to that of optically selected galaxies of similar luminosities and redshifts. These results suggest that the 18um-selected galaxies are a normal population of galaxies.
prompt_few_shot: Using the AKARI mid-infrared camera (IRC) and ground-based optical and near-infrared data, we investigate the multi-wavelength properties of 18 {\mu}m-selected galaxies in the AKARI/IRC monitor field towards the north ecliptic pole (NEP). The sample consists of 36 galaxies with a flux density \ge 0.33 Jy at 18 {\mu}m in an area of 0.62 deg^2, and is complete down to a flux density of 0.55 Jy. The median redshift of the sample is z \approx 0.9. The rest-frame 8 {\mu}m luminosity (\(L_{8\mu m}\)) distribution peaks at log\((L_{8\mu m}/L_{\odot})\) \approx 11.5. The median \((L_{8\mu m}/L_{FIR})\) ratio of the sample is \approx 0.06, which is smaller than that of local ultra-luminous infrared galaxies (\(L_{FIR}\ge 10^{12} L_{\odot}\)). We find that galaxies with higher \((L_{8\mu m}/L_{FIR})\) ratios tend to have redder [3.6] - [24] {\mu}m colors and higher star-formation rates. A comparison with model spectral energy distributions shows that the observed infrared spectral energy distributions are well reproduced by models with moderate starburst ages (\(10^8-10^9\) yr) and high star-formation rates (\(10-100 M_{\odot} yr^{-1}\)). Our results suggest that the majority of the 18 {\mu}m-selected galaxies in the NEP field are luminous starburst galaxies at z \approx 1, powered by star formation rather than an active galactic nucleus.

Our study highlights the importance of multiwavelength observations in understanding the energetics of luminous obscured quasars and their role in shaping the cosmic environment. Overall, our findings contribute valuable new information to the field of quasar research and shed light on the energetic processes driving these enigmatic objects.

title: High Metallicity of the X-Ray Gas up to the Virial Radius of a Binary  Cluster of Galaxies: Evidence of Galactic Superwinds at High-Redshift
direct_prompt: **Abstract**We present X-ray observations of a binary galaxy cluster system at _z_ = 1.067 and measure the gas metallicity up to the virial radius (_r_{200_}) to investigate the impact of galactic superwinds on the enrichment of the intracluster medium (ICM) in the early Universe. The stacked X-ray spectrum shows an elevated metallicity with a mass-weighted average of 0.39 ± 0.11 solar within _r_{200_}, which is significantly higher than the mass-weighted average metallicity within _r_{500_} and also higher than that in other galaxy clusters at similar redshifts. The metallicity profile reveals a flat distribution from the central region out to _r_{200_}, indicating efficient metal mixing in the ICM. The high metallicity and flat metallicity profile can be explained by a scenario in which galactic superwinds play an important role in enriching the ICM. Our result suggests that the enrichment of the ICM by galactic superwinds may have occurred in clusters in the early Universe and can explain the observed high metallicity in some high-redshift clusters.

By making use of XMM-Newton observations, we explore the global metal distribution of a high-redshift (z = 0.44) binary cluster of galaxies. Our results thus support the scenario of galactic winds driven by active galactic nuclei, which can inject metals to the outer regions of the ICM.

Our approach is based on the idea of evolving a population of candidate partition sizes and selecting the best individual according to a fitness function. We evaluate our approach using a dataset of HIV patient data and show that it can significantly improve the performance of rough set-based classification algorithms.

title: Exact dimer ground states for a continuous family of quantum spin chains
direct_prompt: Here is a 6 sentence abstract for the provided article title:Quantum spin chains are a class of interacting quantum many-body systems widely studied in condensed matter physics. In this paper, we consider a continuous family of one-dimensional quantum spin chains parameterized by an anisotropy parameter. By exploiting mappings between spin-1/2 models and fermionic systems, we derive exact analytic expressions for the ground states of these spin chains in the dimerized regime. Specifically, we show that for any value of the anisotropy parameter, the ground states of the chains factorize into singlets formed between nearest neighbor spins when the exchange couplings between even and odd bonds are sufficiently different. We obtain closed-form expressions for the energies and wavefunctions of these exact dimer ground states. Our results provide insights into the equilibrium properties of these quantum spin systems in their lowest-energy dimerized phases.
prompt_few_shot: Here is a 6 sentence abstract for the given title:We study the ground states of a continuous family of quantum spin chains using matrix product states and the exact dimer formalism. The Hamiltonians considered contain nearest neighbor interactions between spins situated on a one dimensional lattice. We find that the ground states of these models can be described exactly as weighted superpositions of dimer coverings of the underlying lattice. An analytic expression is derived for the matrix product states representing the dimer ground states. These generating states are highly degenerate and allow determination of correlation functions in the ground state manifold. The simple structure of the matrix product states also provides insights into the properties of excitations above the dimer ground states.

We find that for a large region of the coupling parameter space, the ground state is a trivial valence bond solid. However, at the boundary between topological and trivial phases, the model reduces to an exactly solvable p-spin Hamiltonian with an extensive ground state degeneracy. This degenerate point corresponds to a multicritical point separating topological and trivial phases. We calculate several physical quantities such as string orders and entanglement entropy to characterize the topological and trivial phases. Our results establish this quantum spin chain family as a prototype system for exploring topological phase transitions in one dimension.

title: Causal inference in longitudinal studies with history-restricted  marginal structural models
direct_prompt: Causal inference in longitudinal studies is often complicated by time-varying confounding. Marginal structural models (MSMs) provide a powerful framework for causal inference in the presence of time-varying confounding. However, traditional MSMs require the assumption of no unmeasured confounding, which may be violated in practice. History-restricted marginal structural models (HRMSMs) are a recently developed extension of MSMs that relaxes the assumption of no unmeasured confounding by restricting the confounding paths to be constant over time. HRMSMs offer a more robust approach to causal inference in longitudinal studies when unmeasured confounding is suspected. In this paper, we provide an introduction to HRMSMs, including the identification assumptions, estimation methods, and inferential procedures. We also discuss the advantages and limitations of HRMSMs compared to traditional MSMs and other causal inference methods. Finally, we illustrate the use of HRMSMs with a real data example.

prompt_SICO: **Abstract**Causal inference is a fundamental goal of many longitudinal studies, but it can be challenging due to the presence of confounding factors and time-varying exposures. Marginal structural models (MSMs) provide a powerful framework for causal inference in longitudinal studies by explicitly considering the time-varying nature of exposures and confounding factors. However, traditional MSMs require strong assumptions, such as no unmeasured confounding and no selection bias.In this paper, we propose a new class of MSMs, called history-restricted MSMs, that relax these assumptions. History-restricted MSMs allow for unmeasured confounding and selection bias, but they require that the outcome be independent of past exposures and confounding factors conditional on the current exposure and past outcomes. We show that history-restricted MSMs can be used to estimate causal effects in a variety of settings, including studies with time-varying exposures, time-varying confounding factors, and studies with missing data. We also provide a simple and efficient algorithm for fitting history-restricted MSMs.We demonstrate the use of history-restricted MSMs in two empirical applications. In the first application, we use history-restricted MSMs to estimate the effect of antiretroviral therapy on mortality in HIV-infected individuals. In the second application, we use history-restricted MSMs to estimate the effect of job training on earnings.Our results suggest that history-restricted MSMs are a promising new tool for causal inference in longitudinal studies. They are relatively easy to fit and can be used to estimate causal effects in a variety of settings.

The which-way information—that is, the information about which hole the photon went through—is not available. direct_prompt: Superhumps are periodic variations in the light curves of some cataclysmic variable stars. In this study, we present comprehensive simulations of superhumps using a sophisticated numerical model. Our model takes into account various physical processes, such as tidal interactions, mass transfer, and accretion disk dynamics. By running simulations with different input parameters, we explore the conditions under which superhumps can arise in accreting binary systems. Our results show that the presence of a tilted accretion disk is crucial for the generation of superhumps. We also find that the mass ratio between the two stars plays a significant role in determining the amplitude and period of the superhump signal. Additionally, we investigate the impact of different viscosity models on the properties of superhumps. Our simulations reveal that high-viscosity models tend to produce shorter and higher-amplitude superhumps compared to low-viscosity models. We also study the evolution of superhumps over time and find that they can exhibit complex behavior, including period variations and amplitude modulations. Overall, our simulations provide valuable insights into the physical mechanisms responsible for the phenomenon of superhumps in cataclysmic variable stars. Our findings contribute to a better understanding of these intriguing astrophysical objects and their underlying physics.

title: Structure of the stationary state of the asymmetric target process
direct_prompt: Here is an 11 sentence abstract for the given academic article title:The asymmetric target process is a nonequilibrium stochastic process with unique long-term dynamical properties. Previous research has investigated various aspects of this process through simulation and analysis but the underlying structure of its stationary state remains poorly understood. In this paper, we develop a theoretical framework to characterize the stationary state that the process converges to over long timescales. Our approach represents the joint distribution of particle positions and occupation times in terms of a set of orthogonal basis functions. We derive expressions for these basis functions and use them to extract quantitative predictions for key properties of the stationary state. Computer simulations confirm that the theoretical description provides an accurate representation of the simulated stationary state. Interestingly, we find the stationary state exhibits spatially asymmetric structure even though the underlying dynamical rules are spatially symmetric. This feature highlights the system's intrinsic inability to sustain detailed balance. More broadly, our work provides new insights into nonequilibrium steady states for stochastic spreading processes far from thermal equilibrium. Finally, the theoretical framework introduced here could potentially be extended to analyze other stochastic systems exhibiting anomalous nonequilibrium behavior.

For inclusive particle production, the factorization has been proven to all orders in the strong coupling constant. However, for dijet production, it is only valid up to next-to-leading order. In this paper, we investigate the high-transverse-momentum dijet production at the LHC in the kt jet algorithm, which is widely used in experimental analyses. We show that the kt factorization is violated for dijet production with large rapidity separation between the two jets. We demonstrate the violation using the kt jet algorithm with different distance measures, including the exclusive kt algorithm and the inclusive kt algorithm. The violation of the kt factorization implies that the collinear factorization approach fails in this case, and the kt jet algorithm is not suitable for studying the high-transverse-momentum dijet production at the LHC. We discuss possible origins of the violation of the kt factorization and propose several methods to improve the kt jet algorithm.

These Kitaev-type spin models have gauged symmetries and are defined on two-dimensional lattices with spin-1/2 degrees of freedom on the edges. In this article, we generalize Kitaev's work by studying spin models defined on odd-dimensional manifolds with gauged global and higher-form symmetries. We show that the emergent gauge fields can be characterized by topological polynomials associated with index theorems. Our models realize symmetry-enriched topological phases protected by the higher-form symmetries. By calculating the indices, we determine the pattern of symmetry fractionalization and identify 't'-type topological invariants distinguishing different spin liquid states. We also demonstrate a bulk-edge correspondence relating the bulk indices to protected gapless modes on the boundary. Our work establishes a mathematical framework linking spin models, gauge theories, and index theorems on odd-dimensional manifolds. This provides a platform for designing topological spin states and understanding their symmetries from a higher-categorical perspective.

title: Closed Bosonic String Field Theory at Quintic Order II: Marginal  Deformations and Effective Potential
direct_prompt: [assistant]: Abstract:We discuss the closed bosonic string field theory at quintic order in a general setting, i.e.  for general values of the background charge Q and dilaton. We derive the first order differential equations for the effective potential and the corresponding equations of motion for the background fields. We show that the quantum effective action is invariant with respect to the field-dependent reparameterizations of the background fields. This symmetry leads to the first order differential equations which are independent of the choice of the  background gauge. The general expressions for the background field equations of motion and the β-functions are presented. For a particular choice of the background gauge, we derive the explicit expressions for the first order differential equations in the presence of marginal deformations. We solve these equations in the small deformation limit and show that there exists an exact solution to all the orders of string perturbation theory for which the background metric is flat and the dilaton is constant.

direct_prompt: In this study, we report the detection of a high-amplitude kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) at approximately 1258 Hz in the ultra-compact X-ray binary 1A 1246-588. The QPO was observed during a pointed observation with the Rossi X-ray Timing Explorer. We analyze the frequency evolution of the QPO during the observation, finding it to be stable over a period of several hours. The high amplitude of the QPO suggests that it is likely associated with the inner accretion disk around the neutron star in the binary system. We compare the properties of this QPO with other known QPOs in similar systems, finding that it falls within the typical frequency range but with a higher amplitude. We discuss possible explanations for the origin of the QPO, including modes of oscillation in the accretion disk or interactions between the disk and the neutron star. Our detection of this high-amplitude QPO adds to the growing body of evidence for the presence of QPOs in ultra-compact X-ray binaries. Further observations and theoretical modeling will be necessary to fully understand the physical mechanisms driving these oscillations. This discovery also highlights the importance of continued monitoring and study of such systems to uncover new insights into the behavior of accreting compact objects.

direct_prompt: In this article, we present a study of photon-jet correlations in proton-proton ($pp$) and proton-antiproton ($p\bar p$) collisions using the STAR detector at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC). The results show a significant correlation between photons and jets in both $pp$ and $p\bar p$ collisions, which suggests a common origin of photons and jets in the fragmentation process. The correlation strength and slope exhibit a dependence on the photon pseudorapidity and transverse momentum, as well as the jet transverse momentum. The $p\bar p$ collision data show a smaller correlation strength than the $pp$ collision data, which may indicate a difference in the fragmentation mechanisms. The results provide new insights into the production mechanisms of photons and jets in hadronic collisions.

Our results include both leading-order (LO) and next-to-leading order (NLO) contributions, and we find that the NLO corrections significantly affect the shapes of the distributions, especially at large transverse momenta. This work contributes to the growing body of research on modified theories of gravity and their implications for observational tests of fundamental physics. title: Obtaining the spacetime metric from cosmological observations
direct_prompt: Here is a 9 sentence abstract for the article titled "Obtaining the spacetime metric from cosmological observations":The geometry of the universe is defined by its spacetime metric. Precisely determining the metric has been an endeavour of cosmologists seeking to understand the structure and evolution of the universe. This paper presents a novel method for directly inferring the spacetime metric from observational cosmological data without relying on solutions to Einstein's field equations. Using a Bayesian approach, we construct a parametrized form for the metric and compute its posterior probability distribution given current cosmological data sets. Our analysis uses supernova luminosity distances, baryon acoustic oscillations, and the cosmic microwave background to constrain the metric. The results provide the first model-independent reconstruction of the spacetime geometry on cosmological scales from observations. Key features of the derived metric agree with the concordance Lambda CDM model while remaining flexible enough to identify possible deviations. This work advances our ability to test general relativity on the largest scales without theoretical assumptions and could reveal new insights into the nature of gravity and dark energy.

direct_prompt: The polarization in the JVAS/CLASS flat-spectrum radio sources: II. A search for aligned radio polarizationsWe present the results of a search for aligned radio polarizations in a complete sample of 224 flat-spectrum radio sources with |b| > 20° selected from the JVAS/CLASS surveys. Our sample consists of 158 compact steep-spectrum (CSS) and 66 GHz-peaked spectrum (GPS) sources. We used archival VLA and ATCA observations at 20 cm and GMRT observations at 610 MHz to estimate the fractional polarization and the electric vector position angle (EVPA) for each source. The fractional polarization is in the range 0.1%–16% at 20 cm, and 0.2%–22% at 610 MHz, with a median of 2.2% and 3.1%, respectively. The EVPAs are distributed randomly with no evidence for large-scale alignment or a preferred direction for the magnetic field. We find that the fractional polarization at 20 cm decreases significantly with increasing spectral index, but there is no clear correlation between the fractional polarization at 610 MHz and the spectral index. We find a significant difference in the median fractional polarization between CSS and GPS sources at 20 cm, but not at 610 MHz. The median EVPA difference between the two polarizations for CSS sources is 12°, while that for GPS sources is 1°. We find no evidence for a correlation between the EVPA difference and any other source property.

Through this analysis, we demonstrate the importance of accurate theoretical predictions for diphoton production in interpreting experimental results and probing the nature of particle interactions at hadron colliders. It is something to look forward to."Signeul believes Scotland "couldn't have asked for anything better" in terms of "getting a little bit of attention around the tournament" by drawing England first up.Her side will then play Portugal, ranked 40th, in Rotterdam on Sunday, 23 July.Their final group game will be against Spain, ranked 14th, in Deventer on Thursday, 27 July."They are two teams we have to watch out for," Signeul told BBC Scotland. "We know they have developed a lot."Spain have had huge success on the youth side and their young players are coming through to the senior team and showing a lot of progress.  So we have two very difficult teams there as well.  It is an interesting and exciting group."It is Scotland's first time at a major finals after 13 failed attempts, having finished runner-up to Iceland in their qualifying campaign.Despite a convincing qualifying campaign in which Scotland won seven and lost one of their eight games, they were beaten 7-0 in a home friendly by Euro hosts the Netherlands in October, underlining the scale of the challenge to progress to the knock-out stages next summer."When you look at the draw and the 16 teams, you realise how big this tournament has become and how many good teams there are in Europe now playing women's football, competing at the highest level," Signeul added."Germany, England, France and Holland are all very, very strong and it will take a lot for us to be able to compete, but we are going to try."Group A: Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark, NorwayGroup B: Germany, Sweden, Russia, ItalyGroup C: France, Iceland, Austria, SwitzerlandGroup D: England, Scotland, Spain, Portugal

human_text: Sushi Kim is a clean and bright place with seats on all two floors. The Korean BBQ buffet is on the second floor and only available on Friday and Saturday evenings starting at 5pm. nnThe service was wonderful and the servers really helpful. The Korean BBQ is buffet style, so you help yourself to the raw proteins and vegetables at the buffet bars and then cook them on your hot plate at your table. It's a really fun and interactive eating experience. There weren't that many choices for proteins, but the choices that were available were all delicious. Protein choices ranged from mussels and shrimps to pork, chicken and beef. My favorite was the bulgogi beef. nnThere were a few things I disliked about the Korean BBQ at Sushi Kim though. First off, they offered no butter or oil for the BBQ. I understand that they are trying to keep things healthy and all, but without any grease, the food was easily burnt. Butter or oil should always be an available option. Secondly, I did not like the design of their hot plates--the interior cooking area was way too tiny so it took forever to cook the food. And finally, they need to add a DESSERT BAR. After eating all that grilled food, I craved something sweet and refreshing. But, Sushi Kim left me hanging. Sushi Kim is already charging a whopping $24 per person--it would be nice if they throw in a dessert bar to sweeten up the deal (pun intended). nnOverall, I'm very thankful there is a Korean BBQ place in Pittsburgh. For being the only Korean BBQ buffet place in the area, it deserves a standing ovation. I had a great time at Sushi Kim and would gladly recommend the Korean BBQ buffet special. Buffet price was a bit high though, so crack open that piggy bank!

The service is usually friendly and efficient, with servers replenishing coffee mugs quickly. Prices are very reasonable for the large portions you get. The dining room is spacious and decorated in a classic diner style with comfy vinyl booths. Windows around the perimeter of the restaurant let in lots of natural light. My favorite thing to order is the banana pecan pancakes which have the perfect balance of sweet and savory flavors. Wash it all down with a fresh squeezed orange juice which is some of the best I've ever tasted. After eating at OPH I always feel fully satisfied and not at all stuffed. It's the perfect place to go to fuel up for a full day of activities on the weekends. Although it can get crowded, the friendly staff keeps service moving at a good pace. I've never had a bad meal during any of my many visits over the years. OPH is a reliable go-to whenever friends or family are visiting from out of town. It's comforting to know this classic breakfast spot will be there.

direct_prompt: Here is a 31 sentence continuation of the review:Upstream is one of the most well-known restaurants in Charlotte. The restaurant sits along the banks of the Catawba River in Uptown Charlotte. Diners are greeted with beautiful views of the flowing water and downtown skyline upon entering. Upstream offers both indoor and outdoor seating depending on preferences and weather. The menu features fresh, local ingredients prepared with creative flair. Dishes showcase the abundance of North and South Carolina with selections like pan-seared trout and pimento cheese grits. The cuisine strikes an excellent balance of refined tastes and approachable favorites. Presentation of the food is just as pleasing to eyes as it is to taste buds. Complimentary biscuits served with apple butter are the ideal start to any meal. For lunch or dinner, the selection of smaller plates allows for sampling multiple dishes. Upstream also has an extensive wine list with Old and New World varietals at a variety of price points. Service is consistently attentive without being overbearing. The atmosphere remains casual despite the upscale fare. On nice evenings, sitting outside provides a serene ambiance enhanced by live jazz. Cocktails showcase seasonal ingredients in refreshing liberations. Desserts satisfy any sweet tooth with choices like buttermilk pie and bread pudding. The restaurant has earned high praise from both locals and visitors alike for its quality, consistency and delightful dining experience overall. Upstream continues to evolve its menu in harmony with the changing seasons. Many patrons return time and again to enjoy favorites or sample new creations. Weekend brunch offers satisfying options for breaking bread with friends and family. Private dining and catering menus cater to all types of events from business lunches to wedding receptions. Those seeking a romantic night out will appreciate Upstream's sophistication without pretense.

The signs in the airport could also be improved, it was not always clear how to get from one place to another. Most of the other passengers waiting around also had long layovers, so the mood was restless. When I finally got to my gate, I was happy to finally be on my way to my final destination. In general, my short visit did not give me a good first impression, but the construction may improve the experience for future travelers. If I have a layover here again in the future, I will make sure to arrive with things to do outside the airport.
human_text: My flight from Tampa let out right near the gate of my connecting flight, which was great and convenient. I ran to the restroom, which was very crowded but understandable. I went into the only open stall, and noticed right away that the post on the back of the door to hang your bags/purses was broken. I had my carry-on bag with me, which is a big cross-body bag that holds my laptop, tablet, phone, etc. So I had to awkwardly hold it on my lap while I did my business, instead of just hanging it up like in most restrooms, especially those at airports. nnHowever the most annoying thing about this airport was that the gates and seating areas were crammed into little corners. Not only making it hard to find a spot to wait, but it was almost impossible to hear them call your flight for boarding since many flights were departing around the same time, lines formed and it was just an absolute mess. The trash cans I saw in the seating area were also overflowing. People tried to throw out plastic cups and the like before their flight and at one point some of it just toppled onto the ground. Overall the experience was unpleasant, I've been to much better airports.
